paragraphs: Some people think it is not bad when heretics stay silent. A heretic is a person with ideas against the official religion. They should first think about this. When heretics are silent, nobody ever discusses their ideas in a fair and full way. Some are wrong and cannot win a discussion. They may stop spreading, but they do not go away.

There is a ban on all thinking that does not end with the official ideas. But this ban does not hurt the minds of heretics the most. It hurts the other people more. Their fear of heresy stops their minds from growing, and it makes their reason weak. Nobody can count how much the world loses. Many people have good minds but shy characters. They are afraid to follow any brave and free idea, because it may lead them to ideas that people call bad or against God. Sometimes we see a man among them with a strong sense of right and a very fine mind. He cannot stop his mind from thinking. All his life, he tries to make his conscience and his reason agree with the official religion. Perhaps he never succeeds, even at the end.

A great thinker must understand one thing. His first duty is to follow his mind to any answer. A person who studies and thinks for himself sometimes makes mistakes. But truth gains more from him than from people with true opinions who never let themselves think.

But free thinking is not only for great thinkers. It is just as important, or more important, for ordinary people. It helps them to grow their minds as much as they can. There have been great thinkers in places where minds were not free, and this may happen again. But in those places there has never been a whole people with active minds, and there never will be. Sometimes a people has come close to this for a short time. This happened because the fear of new ideas stopped for a while. Sometimes people silently agree that nobody can question the main ideas. They think the biggest questions are closed. Then we cannot hope for the high level of thinking that has made some times in history so special. The mind of a people only woke up when people discussed big subjects that made them excited. Only then did even very ordinary people become real thinkers a little.

Europe has had three examples of this. The first was the time just after the Reformation. The second was the movement of new ideas in the second half of the eighteenth century. It was only on the Continent and among educated people. The third was shorter. It was the time of Goethe and Fichte in Germany. These three times had very different opinions. But in all three, people broke free from authority. They threw off an old power over their minds, and no new power had taken its place. The energy of these three times has made Europe what it is now. Every good change in the human mind or in society comes from one of them. But for some time, this energy has seemed almost finished. We cannot expect a new start until we say again that our minds are free.
